eligibility_rationale: Nectar robbery alters floral reward state and is crossed with pollinator access, but the study does not estimate two receiver functions responding to one independently declared plant trait coordinate.

The same nectar-robbing visitors directly cross-pollinate while also reducing legitimate visitor rates. Benefit and cost are coupled in consumer role, not resolved as fixed opposing functions on one plant trait coordinate.

The experiment varies nectar-robbing intensity and measures pollen transfer and fitness consequences; robbery is the imposed interaction state rather than a focal floral trait coordinate receiving two functional responses.
